extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the Israel Journal of Mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and preparation rules for research articles to Israel Journal of Mathematics, covering initial file formats, LaTeX source requirements, figure and table formatting, short title and abstract length, and copyright/exclusivity terms. Targets authors preparing manuscripts for submission and eventual production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission: PDF + cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Initially, authors should send a pdf file of the manuscript, accompanied by a cover letter that includes the full mailing address (not just the email address) and the title of the paper. Papers submitted to the Israel Journal of Mathematics should be sent to iton@math.huji.ac.il addressed to the Managing Editor (Eran London) at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the full postal mailing address in the cover letter (not only email). All submissions will be acknowledged. Use the specified email and postal addressee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract is to be provided, preferably no longer than 150 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the abstract concise and ideally within the 150-word guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide TeX/LaTeX source after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a paper is accepted for publication, the authors will be requested to send a tex / latex file of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the author cannot supply a TeX/LaTeX source file, the paper will be retyped by the journal (implying authors should supply source when possible to avoid retyping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Israel Journal LaTeX style
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should ideally be prepared using the Israel Journal format style which can be downloaded; the site includes a sample file and a guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to adopt the journal's style file and sample as the basis for submissions to match journal formatting and ease production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short title length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors should provide a short title containing at most 40 characters (including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the supplied short title is 40 characters or fewer (counting spaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS subject classifications and keywords policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS subject classifications and keywords are ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on AMS classifications/keywords for editorial routing or emphasis; include them if you wish but be aware the journal ignores them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure format and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be generated using vector graphics (or if bitmap graphics are used, highest possible resolution should be used). Preferably eps or ps format should be used. Figures submitted as pdf (jpg, gif, etc.) are changed to eps. This can cause a quality loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer vector formats (EPS/PS) to avoid rasterization and quality loss; if using bitmaps, supply highest resolution. Avoid submitting formats that will be converted and lose quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change page dimensions or margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should not use commands that change text height and width or margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid LaTeX commands or custom settings that alter page geometry; adhere to the journal's default layout to ensure correct typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wide tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should avoid wide tables. The journal's dimensions are relatively small and so wide tables do not fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tables to fit the journal column/page width; consider splitting or reformatting wide tables to conform to the journal's dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and exclusivity upon submission
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting a manuscript, an author acknowledges that it is not being considered, nor will be submitted elsewhere, and agrees that the sole copyright is transferred to the publisher. This transferal is revoked if and when the publisher decides not to publish the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission implies exclusivity and transfer of copyright to the publisher if accepted. The publisher grants limited rights back to authors (see next entry) but submission should not be simultaneous with other journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author rights after publication (limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher's copyright covers the exclusive right to reproduce and distribute the article by any means. The publisher grants the author the right to distribute a small number of preprints and reprints, to have a preprint available on the Internet and to include the published article in the author's own homepage and in a collection of the author's articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain limited freedoms to share preprints and personal copies on their homepages and collections, and to distribute a small number of reprints; commercial or broader redistribution rights are reserved by the publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication: PDF delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication the pdf file of the published paper is sent to the main author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main author will receive the published PDF; plan distribution or archiving accordingly.
